answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring every identity to lock a non-fungible pigment derived from its private vault into a shared bonding pool. Only agents that continuously attest peer work at the network's zenith of participation recover their stake; each additional fake identity forces the attacker to provision a distinct vault, burn irreversible pigment, and sustain ongoing compute, making large-scale identity farming economically ruinous.
